neighbours.label: perfect-aspect auxiliary context ('have/'ve/has since/been') where a past participle is expected next
fire: Researchers have since confirmed the original findings.
The company has since expanded into three new markets.
Many of the residents have moved away from the valley.
We’ve learned a lot from last year's mistakes.
Once you have tried the recipe, you can adjust the spices.
The old mill has been converted into apartments.
Since then, the town has grown to twice its size.
The volunteers who have completed training will get badges.
quiet: Researchers will soon confirm the original findings.
The company plans to expand into three new markets.
Many of the residents moved away from the valley.
We learn a lot from last year's mistakes.
Once you try the recipe, you can adjust the spices.
The old mill stands empty beside the apartments.
Back then, the town was half its present size.
The volunteers who complete training will get badges.

notes: Broad pole (1.9% at 0.1 max). Output promotes past participles (' developed', ' created'). Near misses are the same sentences in non-perfect tense.
